# Adopting the ssdt-agent workflow in GitHub Copilot for Visual Studio

<!-- Generated by ssdt-agent/scripts/ssdt-agent-package.mjs copilot-apply (the tree carries its own generator; in the source monorepo the tree sits at sidecar/projection/ssdt-agent/). Do not edit by hand; edit the canonical tree or the generator and re-run. -->

This bundle lets a developer working in GitHub Copilot inside Visual Studio drive the ssdt-agent
workflow: state a schema change in plain words, prove it, and open a pull request a reviewer can
approve by reading. The bundle is generated from the canonical tree; do not edit its files by
hand.

## What is in the bundle

- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — the router Copilot reads on every request. It says when to
  use the workflow, the one rule that governs it (prove before you classify), and where the
  skills live.
- `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` — path-scoped notes that attach when a developer opens
  a `.sql` file, a pre- or post-deployment script, or a publish profile. They carry the traps
  that surprise SSDT-new developers and route to the matching skill.
- `.github/agents/*.agent.md` — the three roles (intake, change-author, reviewer) as Copilot
  custom agents, for Visual Studio versions that support them (2026 18.4+).
- `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` — the operation skills and shared-knowledge skills as dispatch
  pointers Copilot matches on (2026 18.5+). Each points into the vendored tree for its full body.
- `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md` — the Visual Studio 2022 entry points: `#prompt:ssdt-intake`,
  `#prompt:ssdt-change-author`, `#prompt:ssdt-review` adopt the same three roles manually.
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/schema-change.md` and
  `.azuredevops/pull_request_template/schema-change.md` — the ten-section schema-change pull
  request template (mirrors `ssdt-agent/skills/author-pr/SKILL.md`), for either host.
- `ssdt-agent/skills/INDEX.md` (generated into the tree itself) — the one-hop dispatch table a
  skills-blind agent reads instead of searching 61 directories.

## Install

0. **Turn custom instructions on — in Visual Studio 2022 they are off by default.** In
   **Tools → Options → GitHub → Copilot → Copilot Chat**, check **Enable custom instructions to
   be loaded from .github/copilot-instructions.md files and added to requests** (in Visual
   Studio 2026 the same setting sits under **All Settings → GitHub → Copilot → Copilot Chat**).
   This one switch gates both the router and the path-scoped instruction files. Then verify, on
   each machine: ask Copilot Chat "what governs schema changes in this repository?" and confirm
   `copilot-instructions.md` appears in the response's **References** list. No reference means
   the switch is off or the file did not load — fix that machine before relying on the workflow.
1. **Vendor the tree.** Copy the whole `ssdt-agent/` directory (the canonical tree) into the
   root of your estate repository, so its path is `ssdt-agent/` at the repository root. The
   skills, agents, and instructions in this bundle reference it there. If you vendor it to a
   different path, adjust the `ssdt-agent/...` references throughout the bundle to match.
   Program history of the source repository is safe to prune from the vendored copy — nothing
   functional cites it: `ASSESSMENT_2026_08_24.md`, `ENABLEMENT_PROGRAM.md`,
   `HANDOFF_SESSION_2026_08_26.md`, `PHASE_2_CURRICULUM.md`, `ACCELERANT_PLAN.md`, and the
   tree's `CLAUDE.md` (source-repo session routing). Keep everything else: the skills cite
   `CONNECTORS.md`, `FINDINGS_AND_CHANGES.md`, `THE_RECORD.md`, `THE_RECORD_FORMS.md`,
   `THE_DECISION_TREE.md`, `PROVING_PATH_WINDOWS.md`, `estate/`, `self-test/`, `sample-prs/`,
   and `proving-ground/` from inside the tree — and `scripts/` + `copilot-package/` are the
   generator and its staging, which keep the bundle regenerable after the tree leaves home.
2. **Copy the `.github/` and `.azuredevops/` bundles.** Merge this bundle's `.github/` and
   `.azuredevops/` directories into your repository's. Where a file already exists, review both
   before overwriting. (After vendoring, `ssdt-agent/scripts/ssdt-agent-package.mjs
   copilot-apply` writes these files in place — it detects the vendored layout.)
3. **Narrow the globs (optional).** The instruction files attach to `**/*.sql`, the deployment
   scripts, and `**/*.publish.xml` across the whole repository. If your SSDT project sits in one
   subfolder, narrow the `applyTo` globs to that folder so the notes attach only where they
   belong.

## What loads on which Visual Studio version

Visual Studio's Copilot support has grown quickly, so the workflow is built to degrade cleanly.
Each rung down still works; the router carries the parts the newer features would have
automated.

- **Best case — Visual Studio 2026, version 18.5 or newer.** Copilot discovers the custom agents
  and the skills automatically, attaches the path-scoped instructions, and reads the router. The
  full workflow is available.
- **Visual Studio 2026, 18.4.** Custom agents work; automatic skill discovery does not. The
  router and the agents carry the instruction to find the matching skill via
  `ssdt-agent/skills/INDEX.md` and read it, so the skills still reach the agent — read rather
  than auto-loaded.
- **Visual Studio 2022, 17.14.** No custom agents and no skills. The router and the path-scoped
  instructions still load (with the step-0 switch on), and they tell Copilot's agent mode to
  adopt a role by reading the agent file and to find the matching skill via the index. The
  prompt files give a clickable entry: `#prompt:ssdt-intake` (or the ➕ reference picker) adopts
  the role without typing the routing by hand. Proving still runs, because it is terminal
  commands the agent runs with your approval.
- **Agent mode turned off, or ask-only Copilot.** Only the router and the manually attached
  instruction files apply. The skills and agents become documents a developer reads. The tree is
  still a usable manual; it is just not driving.

The rung you are on depends on your Visual Studio version and your organization's Copilot policy
— agent mode is gated by an editor-preview-features policy on Copilot Business and Enterprise.
Confirm your version, the policy, and step 0's switch before the week, so you know which rung
you stand on.

## Adopting on Azure DevOps

Visual Studio reads every surface in this bundle from the local checkout, so an Azure DevOps
repository works unchanged — the `.github/` directory name is only a convention. Three
ADO-specific notes:

- **CI check.** GitHub Actions does not run on ADO. Register
  `ssdt-agent/pipelines/ssdt-agent-check.yml` as a pipeline and add it to the default branch's
  build-validation policy, so a pull request that edits the tree or the bundle fails when they
  drift (`copilot-check`).
- **PR template.** ADO reads `.azuredevops/pull_request_template/schema-change.md`; the bundle
  emits it alongside the GitHub copy.
- **What does not follow you to ADO.** GitHub-hosted Copilot features — the coding agent, code
  review's skills, organization-level custom instructions — key off github.com and do not apply
  to an ADO repository. Everything in this bundle is IDE-side and unaffected.

## The Visual Studio 2026 pilot (run before moving anyone)

One champion laptop, Visual Studio 2026 (Community is fine) installed side-by-side with 2022,
the estate solution open. Thirty minutes:

1. The estate `.sqlproj` opens and builds — 2026 carries only the original (classic) SQL project
   format, so a classic project needs no conversion.
2. **Refactor → Rename writes a refactorlog entry.** Non-negotiable; the rename operations
   depend on it.
3. Schema Compare works, if the team uses it.
4. A schema prompt visibly activates a skill from `.github/skills/` — the activation shows in
   the chat.
5. `@intake` appears in the agent picker and adopts the role.
6. Custom-agent tool groups: check whether tools start disabled or reset between turns (a known
   issue on some builds) and note the workaround cost.

All green means that laptop runs the full rung — the same vendored files light up automatically;
the bundle needs no changes. Anything red stays on the 2022 rung and is re-checked on a later
2026 build.

## The prerequisite this bundle cannot provide

The workflow's core move is to prove a change against real-shaped data before classifying it.
That needs a local SQL Server the agent can publish a disposable copy to, and a copy of real Dev
data to publish against. This bundle does not set that up: it is machine setup, and it is the
highest prerequisite. Follow `ssdt-agent/PROVING_PATH_WINDOWS.md` to stand it up, and verify it
before the team leans on the workflow. Until proving runs, the router tells the agent to stop and
say so, rather than guess from the SQL text.

## Keeping the bundle in sync

The bundle is generated from the canonical tree by the tree's own generator:

```
node ssdt-agent/scripts/ssdt-agent-package.mjs copilot-apply
```

(In the source monorepo the tree sits at `sidecar/projection/ssdt-agent/`; the command is the
same — paths resolve from the script's location.) In the source repo this stages the bundle into
`ssdt-agent/copilot-package/`; in a vendored estate repository the generator detects the layout
and also writes the `.github/` and `.azuredevops/` files in place at the repository root.
`copilot-check` verifies both. The `packaging` gate runs it in the source repo's CI;
`ssdt-agent/pipelines/ssdt-agent-check.yml` runs it on ADO.

Bundle fingerprint: `75f4e217a22d` — a content hash over the generator and every source
file. It changes exactly when regeneration is due, so a stale vendored bundle is detectable at a
glance.

## What is not yet verified

These parts follow current Microsoft and GitHub documentation but have not been run on the
team's actual Visual Studio build. Confirm them on day one:

- That the exact Visual Studio build in use discovers skills from `.github/skills/` and loads the
  custom agents.
- That Copilot's agent mode reads a vendored skill file when the router tells it to, on the older
  rungs — including when the solution is not at the repository root (the pointers say "from the
  repository root" for exactly this case).
- That `#prompt:` attaches the prompt files on the team's 2022 build.
- Whether restricting each agent's tools is worth doing. This bundle leaves the tools unset (the
  default toolset), because Visual Studio's tool names vary by build.
